For Applicants : Shri Sanjay Bahirani, Advocate.
For Respondents : Shri Vijay Sundaram, Panel Lawyer /State  ORDER (Delivered on this Day of 7th January, 2016)

The applicants have challenged the order dated 04/02/2010 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Gwalior in Criminal Case No. 6196/2006,
whereby, charges of offence under section 16(1)(a)(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (in short "PF Act") were framed against the applicants.
2.
The facts of the case in short are that the applicants were found selling some Papad, etc.

The Food Inspector found that the Papad sold by the applicants were adulterated and misbranded and,
therefore, a complaint was filed.
3.
After hearing submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the Judicial Magistrate First Class has passed the impugned order dated 04/02/2010 and charges were framed.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the material available on record.

5. It would be made clear that at the time of framing of charge, it should be considered by the trial court that if any rebuttal evidence is not produced by the accused and if he can be convicted of particular offence then charge of that offence shall be framed.

In this case, the grievance of the Prashant Agrawal vs Deputy Director on 6 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177551732/
1 applicants is that no standard has been fixed in the PF Act relating to Papad and, therefore, the report of the concerned Laboratory cannot be accepted that the Papad was adulterated.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
At present there is a report from the recognized Laboratory that the Papad sample was found adulterated and,
therefore, it is for the applicants to cross examine the concerned analyst and to establish that the sample was not adulterated.
Such arguments cannot be accepted at the stage of framing of charge.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has also submitted that the sample could not be said to be misbranded in the light of judgment passed by Punjab and Haryana High Court in the case of Om Prakash vs. State of Punjab reported in 2000 (2) FAC 253.

entities.text: Om Prakash vs. State of Punjab reported in 2000 (2) FAC 253
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Again it is to be mentioned here that right to defend the case is available with the applicants, at this stage prima facie it cannot be said that the sample was not misbranded.
7. On the basis of aforesaid discussions, no illegality or perversity is found in the impugned order passed by the trial court relating to framing of charge.
Hence, there is no substance in the present criminal revision.
8. Consequently, the present criminal revision filed by the applicants is hereby dismissed.
9. Copy of this order be sent to the court below along with its record with information that there is no stay in the case and the trial court shall proceed with the case as early as possible.
(N.K. GUPTA) JUDGE Durgekar*
